description: The misty highlands of Ethiopia. The obelisks (stelae) of Aksum rise up through the mist. Lush green terraces.
text_content: High in the mountains of East Africa, the Kingdom of Aksum touched the clouds. It was a rich land of trade and ivory.

description: The port of Adulis on the Red Sea. Ships are being loaded with elephant tusks and gold. Diverse traders are bargaining.
text_content: Aksum was powerful. It controlled the Red Sea ports. Ships from India and Rome came to buy its goods.

description: Two young boys standing nervously before the King of Aksum. The court is lavish, filled with gold and leopard skins.
text_content: One day, two Christian boys from Syria, Frumentius and Aedesius, were shipwrecked. They were taken to the King's palace.

description: Frumentius teaching a young Prince Ezana. They are looking at a scroll. The atmosphere is warm and mentorship-focused.
text_content: The boys were smart and kind. They helped the Queen raise her young son, Ezana, who would become the King.

description: King Ezana, now an adult, sitting on his throne deep in thought. A cross is visible in the background design.
text_content: Frumentius told Ezana about Jesus. When Ezana grew up and became King, he did something amazing.

description: Close up of a gold Aksumite coin. On one side, the face of Ezana. On the other, a distinct Cross. The metal glints in the light.
text_content: For years, the coins of Aksum showed the sun and moon gods. But Ezana changed them. He put the Cross of Christ on the coins!

description: A public ceremony where King Ezana is proclaiming his faith. A large stone tablet with inscriptions (Greek, Sabaean, Ge'ez) stands nearby.
text_content: He declared, 'I will rule by the power of the Lord of Heaven.' Aksum became one of the first Christian kingdoms in the world.

description: The monastery of Debre Damo atop a flat-topped mountain (amba). Monks are climbing up a rope to get to it.
text_content: Monks called the 'Nine Saints' came to Aksum. They built monasteries on top of steep cliffs where they were safe to pray.

description: A monk writing in a heavy, leather-bound book. He is using red and black ink to write the Ge'ez script artfully.
text_content: They translated the Bible into Ge'ez, the language of the people. Now everyone could hear the Word of God.

description: A procession of Ethiopian priests carrying ceremonial crosses and colorful umbrellas. The landscape is mountainous and green.
text_content: Aksum declined later, but the faith did not die. It moved deeper into the mountains, kept safe by the people.

description: A child's hand holding an ancient Aksumite coin against the backdrop of a modern Ethiopian church.
text_content: King Ezana’s coins are small, but they tell a huge story of a King who chose the Cross.

description: A parchment map of the Horn of Africa/Ethiopia. It marks 'Aksum', 'Adulis', and the 'Blue Nile'. Mountains are drawn in relief.
text_content: Map: The Highland Kingdom. This map shows the Red Sea and the mountains of Ethiopia. Aksum is the capital in the north.
